name: Planar pin hinges (all axes parallel)
mechanism: Rigid links joined by pins whose axes are all parallel, so the chain bends in one plane only; two antagonistic tendons per plane (or one tendon + return spring).
print_notes: Print knuckles flat so the pin bore axis is vertical (round holes, loads in-plane); 0.3-0.5 mm radial pin clearance for FDM; print-in-place hinges need >=0.4 mm gap; pin knuckles crack along layers if the bore is printed horizontally.
non_printed_parts: steel pins / M2-M3 bolts or 1.75 mm filament as pins
known_issues: only planar motion -> needs a base yaw servo for 3D reach
pin backlash accumulates over many links
pins bend/wear under cycling (seen in printed Sarrus arm)

sources.title: Multi-material 3D printed tendon-driven continuum segment (Leeds, ICRA preprint)
sources.what_it_supports: Vertebrae on Tango+ backbone; v0.2 soft hinges alternated 90 deg (~15 deg/vertebra, 135 deg total); keyed vertebrae cut torsional play 5.6->1.4 deg/vertebra; payload 0.4-1.3 kg; key-base fracture under torsion; nylon then 0.7 mm braided steel tendons

sources.title: Sarrus linkage aerial drone arm (Idaho State Univ. robotics lab)
sources.what_it_supports: Stacked Sarrus links, ABS, 10.2 -> 33 cm (~3.2:1), ~450 g; torsion springs + single cable; pins bent/failed after dozens of cycles; singularity at full extension

source_note: No source dedicated to an all-parallel printed pin-hinge tentacle was verified; Leeds v0.2 (single-DOF hinges, ~15 deg each) and the ISU Sarrus arm (pin bending/failure) are indirect evidence. Range is engineering estimate.

name: Alternating 90-degree pin hinges (snake-robot style)
mechanism: Single-axis hinges whose axes alternate by 90 deg along the chain, so pairs of joints approximate a universal joint; 2 antagonistic tendon pairs give spatial bending.
print_notes: FDM equivalent of Leeds design: print vertebrae separately with pin or key/keyway; keys fracture at base under torsion, so add fillets and print with layers perpendicular to key shear; keep pin bores vertical.
known_issues: torsional play per vertebra (5.6 deg measured -> 1.4 deg with tighter keys)
anisotropic bending (diagonal directions need both pairs)
tendon-link collision limits roll range (TENDRIM +/-60 deg)
gearbox stripping before stall in Leeds tests

sources.title: Multi-material 3D printed tendon-driven continuum segment (Leeds, ICRA preprint)
sources.what_it_supports: Vertebrae on Tango+ backbone; v0.2 soft hinges alternated 90 deg (~15 deg/vertebra, 135 deg total); keyed vertebrae cut torsional play 5.6->1.4 deg/vertebra; payload 0.4-1.3 kg; key-base fracture under torsion; nylon then 0.7 mm braided steel tendons

sources.title: New 3D printed continuum soft robot can lift 3 pounds (3DPrint.com)
sources.what_it_supports: Popular summary of the Leeds segment: 4 tendons, interlocking vertebrae, 1300 g payload, ~10 deg/s under max load

sources.title: Design of the new modular tendon-driven manipulator TENDRIM (TU Braunschweig)
sources.what_it_supports: Bearing-based pitch+roll joints per module (universal-joint equivalent); working range ~120 deg pitch, +/-60 deg roll limited by tendon-link collision; all tendons must stay in tension

name: Universal / Cardan joints
mechanism: Cross-pin (or tubular synovial) universal joints between discs give pitch and yaw at one location while blocking twist; tendons through disc holes drive bending.
print_notes: U-CAAMS printed its U-joint backbone in PLA; print yokes with bores vertical, cross-pin as metal pin; 0.2-0.3 mm clearance; yoke ears are weak across layers - orient so bending load is in-plane; add radial springs for shape recovery.
known_issues: good torsional stiffness (major advantage on a drone vs NiTi backbone)
self-weight sag and gravity-driven in-plane error
per-joint angle limit stops tight curling

sources.title: U-Joint CAAMS: universal-joint continuum manipulator for aerial manipulation (arXiv 2607.03321)
sources.what_it_supports: Drone-mounted PLA-printed tubular U-joint backbone + radial helical springs, 3x1 mm steel tendons, 3x Dynamixel XL430; arm 430 g; bending kept <180 deg to avoid props; 2.5-45x lower out-of-plane error under downwash than NiTi backbone; gravity sag in-plane

sources.title: Universal-jointed tendon-driven continuum robot (arXiv 2409.13165)
sources.what_it_supports: Synovial U-joint laser-cut from tube with open centre channel; bending-angle limit is a design parameter; helical/parallel tendon routing; tendon friction must be modelled

sources.title: A DIY tentacle bot right out of Doctor Octopus' lab (Hackster)
sources.what_it_supports: Hobby 10-disk tentacle with small universal joints + printed adapters, Kevlar strings, 2 servos; U-joints block twist; string slipped on pulleys until wheels redesigned

source_note: Per-joint range not reported numerically in sources; 20-45 deg is an engineering estimate typical of U-joint geometry.

name: Printed ball-and-socket (snap fit / print-in-place)
mechanism: Spherical ball in a socket (or discs riding on balls threaded on an elastic core) gives 2 bend + free axial rotation; tendons through disc holes bend the chain.
print_notes: Print-in-place needs ~0.2 mm clearance and may stick; snap-fit sockets should be PETG/nylon (PLA cracks); print sockets with opening facing up; layer lines on the ball add stick-slip - sand or use a bought ball/bead.
known_issues: no torsional constraint -> chain twists unless tendons or keys resist it
redundant chain not suited to precise position control

sources.title: Tendon-driven continuum robot with ball joints (ROBOMECH Journal 2024)
sources.what_it_supports: 8 PLA discs + 7 x 20 mm wooden balls on rubber string, 3 tendons at 120 deg, SG90 servos, 270 mm/80 g, ~190 g payload; per-joint max 2*theta (~97 deg derived from geometry); CR-10 printed

sources.title: A servo powered robotic arm, but like you've never seen before (Hackaday 2018)
sources.what_it_supports: 8 printed ball-joint segments, 16 remote RC servos, fishing line routed in tubing (Bowden) to decouple joints

sources.title: 3D printed ball joints (Fab Academy 2024, week 05)
sources.what_it_supports: Print-in-place ball joint with -0.2 mm cavity clearance; may stick depending on printer tolerance

source_note: 97 deg is derived from the ROBOMECH geometry (2*asin(0.75)), not a stated measurement; 35 mm is the ROBOMECH ball spacing (pitch).

name: Magnetic ball joints
mechanism: A steel ball held to a seat by a permanent magnet (or a chain of magnetised spheres) forms a self-retaining spherical joint that separates instead of breaking under overload.
print_notes: Housings and seats print easily; magnet pockets need ~0.1-0.2 mm press fit or glue; keep magnets away from flight controller compass.
known_issues: holding force limited (~3 kg per RepRap joint) -> joint pops apart under tentacle bending moments

sources.title: Magnet joint (RepRap wiki)
sources.what_it_supports: Magnet+steel-ball joints ~3 kg holding force each; magnetised-ball pole misalignment -> use cylinder magnet + plain steel ball

sources.title: Ball chain robots (Pittiglio, Mencattelli, Dupont; arXiv 2302.03728)
sources.what_it_supports: Chain of permanently magnetised spheres in polymer skin bends to very small radii; steered by external field (not tendons)

sources.title: CN105522588A Magnetic ball-joint robot (Google Patents)
sources.what_it_supports: Ball-cup joint held/driven by windings + permanent magnets; 3-DOF from one joint; single-magnet version loses axial rotation

name: Rolling-contact joints (cam / CORE style) with straps or cables
mechanism: Two convex cam surfaces roll on each other without slip, constrained by crossed flexure straps or cables; rotation axis moves with contact point and tendon length can stay constant.
print_notes: Cams print well in PLA/PETG; monolithic flexure straps (0.4 mm) are marginal on FDM - use TPU or separate Dyneema/steel straps; cam surfaces printed with layers along the rolling direction to avoid ridges.
known_issues: cam slip if strap tension lost

sources.title: Monolithic compliant rolling-contact joint tendon manipulator (PMC8354933)
sources.what_it_supports: Half-cylinder cams + 4 x 0.4 mm flexure straps, SLS PA2200, 10.6 mm discs; joint >180 deg in tests; 8 joints give 180 deg; constant tendon length; strap stress near/above 50 MPa; breaks at 5 N transverse

sources.title: Rolling-joint design optimization for tendon driven snake-like surgical robots (Imperial Spiral)
sources.what_it_supports: 3D printed serial rolling joints; tendon-joint collision limits joint angle; 0.9 mm repeatability, 5.6 N force

sources.title: Tendon-driven rolling-contact mechanism model (arXiv 2409.00616)
sources.what_it_supports: Planar 5-link rolling-contact prototype (~20 mm links), 0.28 mm PE braid in PTFE tubes; tendon friction -> hysteresis, 2-4 mm tip error

source_note: 22 deg/joint derived from 180 deg over 8 joints in PMC8354933; single test joints exceeded 180 deg.

name: 2-axis / spherical rolling contact joints
mechanism: Spherical surfaces roll on each other (or stacked orthogonal pulleyless rolling units) giving 2-DOF rolling bending with no spin about the contact normal.
print_notes: Spherical rolling surfaces need smooth finish - print with fine layers or sand; constraining straps/cables in 2 axes is fiddly; stacked orthogonal 1-D rolling units are easier to print than true spherical rollers.
known_issues: complex tendon routing to keep length constant in both axes

sources.title: Kinematics of spherical rolling contact joint and manipulator (FreeBOT, freeformrobotics.org)
sources.what_it_supports: 2-DOF spherical rolling contact joint (no spin about normal); magnet-held 68 mm iron spheres; EVA foam for friction, foam deformation -> slip

sources.title: Discrete bending joint using multiple unit PREF joints for isotropic 2-DOF motion (KNU)
sources.what_it_supports: Stacked pulleyless rolling units give 2-DOF isotropic discrete bending; stacking order matters

name: Gear-meshed rolling joints
mechanism: Rolling surfaces carry gear teeth (single tooth or partial gears / geared anti-parallelograms) so the links cannot slip while rolling; doubles effective angle per pivot pair.
print_notes: Partial gears print well with module >=1 mm; print teeth flat on the bed; add side plates/links to hold mesh; PETG or nylon for wear.
known_issues: no-slip and high torsional stiffness (steel proto 3 N*m)
added weight vs plain rolling joint
hobby build needs reinforcement and droops under load

sources.title: Design and analysis of a rolling joint based on gear tooth for continuum robot (BUAA, ICIRA 2021)
sources.what_it_supports: Single gear tooth + rolling surfaces at pitch diameter: no slip, low friction, high torsional stiffness (steel proto: 1000 N axial, 3 N*m torsion)

sources.title: A tentacle that's a work of art (Hackaday 2020)
sources.what_it_supports: Hobby 3D-printed tentacle of anti-parallelogram units synchronised by gears (geared rolling equivalent), cable winches; ~500 g handling estimated by commenter

sources.title: Tendon-driven rolling-contact mechanism model (arXiv 2409.00616)
sources.what_it_supports: Planar 5-link rolling-contact prototype (~20 mm links), 0.28 mm PE braid in PTFE tubes; tendon friction -> hysteresis, 2-4 mm tip error

name: Cross-axis (X) flexural pivots
mechanism: Two thin leaf flexures crossing in an X between two bodies give a pivot with a near-fixed centre and higher off-axis stiffness than a single leaf.
print_notes: Print leaves vertical so they consist of continuous perimeters (not stacked layers in bending); 0.1 mm layers for lattice hinges; supports damage thin hinges; PLA leaves fatigue/creep - prefer PETG, nylon or PP.
known_issues: limited angle before yield in PLA

sources.title: Compliant cross-axis joints with 3D-printed lattice flexures (Applied Sciences 12(13):6635)
sources.what_it_supports: FDM PLA cross-axis pivots; lattice hinges 2-10x more deflection than solid; support removal damaged hinges; parasitic twist from asymmetric lattices

source_note: Source reports displacement not angle; 10-40 deg is typical cross-spring pivot range from general practice.

name: Notch / living-hinge flexures (circular, leaf) in PETG/TPU/PP
mechanism: A locally thinned section (notch, leaf or metamaterial cell) between rigid segments bends elastically to form a monolithic joint; tendons on each side.
print_notes: Orient so the hinge is bent along the perimeters, never across layer lines (delamination); TPU print slow (20-30 mm/s), no retraction issues with direct drive; PP living hinges need hinge flexed right after printing; PLA hinges crack within tens-hundreds of cycles.

sources.title: Bioinspired 3D printable flexure joint with cellular metamaterial architecture (PMC10236482)
sources.what_it_supports: Monolithic FDM TPU 87A flexure joint ~95-110 deg range, 3-stage stiffness; no fatigue data

sources.title: Monolithic TPU flexure joints for confined-space tendon-driven robotic arms (Univ. Moratuwa)
sources.what_it_supports: FDM TPU flexure joint: max 29.2 deg at 15.5 N, linear force-displacement

sources.title: Monolithic compliant rolling-contact joint tendon manipulator (PMC8354933)
sources.what_it_supports: Half-cylinder cams + 4 x 0.4 mm flexure straps, SLS PA2200, 10.6 mm discs; joint >180 deg in tests; 8 joints give 180 deg; constant tendon length; strap stress near/above 50 MPa; breaks at 5 N transverse

name: Two orthogonal notch flexures per segment
mechanism: Each segment has two notch flexures at 90 deg (stacked or alternating), giving 2-axis bending from a monolithic print; essentially the compliant version of alternating hinges.
print_notes: Print the whole chain vertically in TPU or PETG so notches are bent along perimeters; one of the two notch axes will be bent across layer lines if printed horizontally - avoid.

sources.title: Multi-material 3D printed tendon-driven continuum segment (Leeds, ICRA preprint)
sources.what_it_supports: Vertebrae on Tango+ backbone; v0.2 soft hinges alternated 90 deg (~15 deg/vertebra, 135 deg total); keyed vertebrae cut torsional play 5.6->1.4 deg/vertebra; payload 0.4-1.3 kg; key-base fracture under torsion; nylon then 0.7 mm braided steel tendons

sources.title: Notched continuum robot for orthopaedic surgery (Frontiers Bioeng. 2024, 10.3389/fbioe.2024.1470069)
sources.what_it_supports: Nitinol tube with symmetric rectangular notches, 2 cables, planar bending; 3D-printed nylon prototype 66 mm with 15 notches; rounded notch corners to cut stress concentration

source_note: Leeds v0.2 alternated soft hinges at 90 deg (~15 deg/vertebra); no FDM orthogonal-notch tentacle verified.

name: Vertebrae/discs on central elastic backbone (classic tendon-driven continuum)
mechanism: Spacer discs fixed along a flexible backbone (NiTi rod, spring, TPU rod or elastomer) guide 3-4 tendons; pulling tendons bends the segment near constant curvature.
print_notes: Discs print flat; tendon holes drilled/reamed or lined with PTFE; TPU backbone print at 100% infill, square section prints better than round; friction-fit discs to backbone.
non_printed_parts: backbone rod (NiTi/spring steel) if not TPU

sources.title: Tendon-driven continuum robots 101 (Open Continuum Robotics, U Toronto)
sources.what_it_supports: Spacer-disk vs lumen designs; >=3 tendons for spatial bending; disk-tendon friction, tendon slack/backlash, one motor set per segment

sources.title: Tendon-actuated robots with a tapered flexible polymer backbone (arXiv 2603.19124)
sources.what_it_supports: FDM TPU 95A backbone (100% infill, square section, 34.5 cm) + 10 PLA discs on Bambu X1C; 3 tendons, 2-25 N; TPU nonlinearity/FDM anisotropy -> tension-scheduled modulus

sources.title: Reducing actuator requirements in continuum robots through optimized cable routing (Case et al. 2018, Yale)
sources.url: https://www.eng.yale.edu/Faboratory/publications/journal/2018/Case et al. - 2018 - Reducing Actuator Requirements in Continuum Robots through Optimized Cable Routing.pdf
sources.what_it_supports: Dragon Skin 10 segments + PLA vertebrae with fishing-line cables over steel guide rods; crossing routing cuts actuator count 12->8; 30-47 mm tip error from friction

source_note: Range is per section (whole segment), not per disc.

name: Single superelastic/steel spring backbone with spacer discs
mechanism: One NiTi or spring-steel rod/spring provides the elastic restoring force; printed spacer discs carry 3-4 tendons; used on existing aerial continuum manipulators.
dof_per_joint: 2 bend per section (+ extension/twist in some designs)
print_notes: Discs are printed (PLA) and epoxied/friction-fit to the rod; NiTi must be bought; rod must not be bent past superelastic strain.
known_issues: thin NiTi backbone is torsionally weak -> out-of-plane errors under drone downwash
few discs -> shape deviates from arc
rod buckling under high tendon tension

sources.title: Tilt-X aerial continuum manipulator (arXiv 2602.23576)
sources.what_it_supports: Superelastic NiTi backbone, PLA disks, Spectra cables, 20 mm dia, 590 mm reach on X500 quad; downwash sensitivity; actuators at hub keep CoG fixed

sources.title: A modular continuum manipulator for aerial manipulation and perching (arXiv 2206.06246)
sources.what_it_supports: NiTi backbone + 9 PLA printed disks, 4 fishing-wire tendons, 4x XL430; 420 g incl. actuation; not yet flown

sources.title: FAS - a fully actuated segment for tendon-driven continuum robots (Frontiers Robot. AI 2022)
sources.what_it_supports: 0.635 mm NiTi backbone, 12 floating 7 mm disks spaced by ring magnets; bend+extend+twist; few disks -> shape deviation

name: Notched / slotted tube continuum
mechanism: A tube with repeated symmetric or asymmetric notches bends where material is removed; a tendon (asymmetric) or tendon pair (symmetric) bends it.
dof_per_joint: 1 bend (planar) or 2 with rotated notch rows
print_notes: Printable as a vertical TPU/nylon/PETG tube with notches; notch roots must be filleted; scale for a drone tentacle (20-40 mm dia) makes this effectively a notch-flexure tentacle.
known_issues: small range per notch, many notches needed

sources.title: Notched continuum robot for orthopaedic surgery (Frontiers Bioeng. 2024, 10.3389/fbioe.2024.1470069)
sources.what_it_supports: Nitinol tube with symmetric rectangular notches, 2 cables, planar bending; 3D-printed nylon prototype 66 mm with 15 notches; rounded notch corners to cut stress concentration

sources.title: Universal-jointed tendon-driven continuum robot (arXiv 2409.13165)
sources.what_it_supports: Synovial U-joint laser-cut from tube with open centre channel; bending-angle limit is a design parameter; helical/parallel tendon routing; tendon friction must be modelled

name: One-piece printed TPU tentacle with tendon channels
mechanism: Entire tapered tentacle printed as one TPU part (solid core, ribs or wedge units) with integral tendon channels; bends by elastic deformation.
print_notes: Direct-drive extruder, slow speed, 100% infill for backbone; print vertically or in segments joined with dovetails (SpiRobs printed 1 m arm in 4 parts); square section prints more reliably; tendon channels >=1.5 mm, ream after printing.
known_issues: channel friction in TPU is high
tall TPU prints wobble; bed size (256 mm) forces segmented print

sources.title: Tendon-actuated robots with a tapered flexible polymer backbone (arXiv 2603.19124)
sources.what_it_supports: FDM TPU 95A backbone (100% infill, square section, 34.5 cm) + 10 PLA discs on Bambu X1C; 3 tendons, 2-25 N; TPU nonlinearity/FDM anisotropy -> tension-scheduled modulus

sources.title: SpiRobs full paper (arXiv 2303.09861 PDF)
sources.what_it_supports: Wedge units from log spiral (dtheta=30 deg), taper 5-15 deg, eTPU-95A on Bambu FDM, UHMWPE cables; 24 units/45 cm (2 cables), 42 units/1 m (3 cables, 5-120 mm dia); elastic layer 5-10% width; thin layers self-collide/buckle

sources.title: Monolithic TPU flexure joints for confined-space tendon-driven robotic arms (Univ. Moratuwa)
sources.what_it_supports: FDM TPU flexure joint: max 29.2 deg at 15.5 N, linear force-displacement

name: Logarithmic-spiral wedge segment tentacles (SpiRobs)
mechanism: Wedge units sized by a logarithmic spiral share a thin elastic spine; 2-3 cables curl the body into a tight log spiral where neighbouring wedges touch, wrapping objects octopus-style.
dof_per_joint: 1 bend (2 cables) or 2 bend (3 cables), per wedge gap
print_notes: Print in TPU 95A; elastic spine 5% (2-cable) to 10% (3-cable) of unit width; long arms printed in pieces joined by dovetails; 256 mm bed fits a ~25 cm 15-deg-taper arm in one go.
known_issues: thin spine self-collides and buckles under antagonistic loads
thick spine needs much higher cable force (up to 60-100 N)
curvature fixed by geometry (radius shrinks to tip)

sources.title: SpiRobs full paper (arXiv 2303.09861 PDF)
sources.what_it_supports: Wedge units from log spiral (dtheta=30 deg), taper 5-15 deg, eTPU-95A on Bambu FDM, UHMWPE cables; 24 units/45 cm (2 cables), 42 units/1 m (3 cables, 5-120 mm dia); elastic layer 5-10% width; thin layers self-collide/buckle

sources.title: SpiRobs: logarithmic spiral-shaped robots (arXiv 2303.09861, abstract)
sources.what_it_supports: Octopus-inspired log-spiral robots; mm to 1 m scales; grasp up to 260x self-weight; cheap fabrication

source_note: Per-gap range approx equal to the 30 deg log-spiral step closing; 15-30 deg is derived from design parameters, not measured.

name: Kresling origami modules
mechanism: Twisted-polygon fold pattern couples axial contraction with rotation; differential actuation of facets/pouches adds bending; can be bistable.
print_notes: Thin TPU or PETG panels with TPU living-hinge creases can be printed flat then folded, or printed as sandwich plates; crease fatigue is the main failure.
known_issues: twist coupled to contraction (needs opposite-handed stacks)
low bending stiffness in folded state

sources.title: Bending stiffness of generalized Kresling modules for robotic manipulation (NSF PAR)
sources.what_it_supports: Kresling bending stiffness switches between stable states; 3D-printed sandwich-plate cores; coupled twist complicates use

sources.title: Origami-inspired universally deformable module (TechXplore, Nature Comms 2023)
sources.what_it_supports: Two-level opposite-handed Kresling, pneumatic (vacuum + pouches), 7 motion modes; classic Kresling couples twist and contraction

name: Yoshimura / waterbomb origami continuum segments
mechanism: Collapsible folded tubes (Yoshimura diamond pattern or waterbomb bases) act as tendon-guided bellows that bend and contract; often stiffened by a spring or NiTi backbone.
print_notes: Normally laser-cut film; FDM alternative is thin PETG panels with TPU hinges (multi-material) or printing TPU directly as a thin folded surface; creases fatigue.
known_issues: low torsional strength (film twisted at ~0.43 N*m)

sources.title: Origami continuum manipulation module (Santoso et al., IROS 2017, WPI)
sources.what_it_supports: Yoshimura PET module: 2 bend + 1 axial DOF, 35.5 deg at 45 mm arc, 65->30 mm collapse, 110 g; 5 mil film twists at ~0.43 N*m

sources.title: An extensible continuum robot with integrated origami parallel modules (academia.edu)
sources.what_it_supports: Waterbomb-base origami parallel modules on steel spring backbone; up to 45 deg/module, >180 deg over 6 modules; crease fatigue

sources.title: Design of lightweight and extensible tendon-driven continuum robot using origami (Kyung Hee)
sources.what_it_supports: Paper origami tendon guides on NiTi backbone: >10x extension, +/-167 deg yaw/pitch, 21.9 g

name: Tensegrity / cable-strut segments
mechanism: Rigid struts held in a pretensioned cable network; shortening active cables bends the module while it remains compliant and impact tolerant.
print_notes: Nodes/vertebrae print easily; struts best as carbon rod; cable tensioning by hand is tedious and variable.
known_issues: many cables to tension and maintain

sources.title: DeXteR dexterous continuum tensegrity manipulator (NSF PAR)
sources.what_it_supports: Vertebra modules of 2 curved links + 12 strings; 10 modules built; slack/taut string switching -> nonlinear dynamics

sources.title: Tensegrity manipulator TM-40 estimation and control (arXiv 2603.05976)
sources.what_it_supports: 5 class-1 modules, CFRP struts, Kevlar passive cables, pneumatic active cables; 1.16 m; deep-bend estimation errors

sources.title: Flexible actuated tensegrity spine for quadrupeds (arXiv 1804.06527)
sources.what_it_supports: 3D-printed tetrahedral vertebrae, laser-cut silicone lattice, hand-set cable tension; asymmetric parasitic bending

name: Coil-spring joints / helical compliant segments
mechanism: A coil spring between rigid adaptors (or around a backbone) acts as an omnidirectional bending joint and restoring element; tendons pass outside or through it.
print_notes: Adaptors print easily; printed TPU/PETG helices possible but buy springs for consistency; spring ends need clamping pockets.
known_issues: poor torsional stiffness -> tangling and flipping

sources.title: Tendon-driven compliant snake robot with global bending and twisting (arXiv 2407.16054)
sources.what_it_supports: Coil-spring continuum joints over torque-coil backbone + NiTi rod anti-buckling; poor torsional stiffness -> tangling/flipping; friction tension loss along length

sources.title: U-Joint CAAMS: universal-joint continuum manipulator for aerial manipulation (arXiv 2607.03321)
sources.what_it_supports: Drone-mounted PLA-printed tubular U-joint backbone + radial helical springs, 3x1 mm steel tendons, 3x Dynamixel XL430; arm 430 g; bending kept <180 deg to avoid props; 2.5-45x lower out-of-plane error under downwash than NiTi backbone; gravity sag in-plane

sources.title: An extensible continuum robot with integrated origami parallel modules (academia.edu)
sources.what_it_supports: Waterbomb-base origami parallel modules on steel spring backbone; up to 45 deg/module, >180 deg over 6 modules; crease fatigue

name: Printed/molded bellows soft actuators (PneuNet, fiber-reinforced)
mechanism: Elastomer chambers with an inextensible strain layer (PneuNet) or fiber wrapping bend when pressurised; no tendons needed.
dof_per_joint: 1 bend per actuator (2-3 chambers give 2 bend)
print_notes: Molds print well in PLA; direct TPU printing of bellows is possible but leak-prone at layer seams - needs sealing; silicone casting needs vacuum degassing.
known_issues: leaks at tube entry and bubbles
pump + valves add mass to a drone

sources.title: PneuNet actuators (Soft Robotics Toolkit)
sources.what_it_supports: Ecoflex 0030/0050 two-layer molded chambers with nylon strain layer; bubbles, uneven cure, tube-entry leaks

sources.title: Mechanically programmable bend radius for fiber-reinforced soft actuators (Harvard Biodesign)
sources.what_it_supports: Fiber-reinforced elastomer bender; conformal covering programs bend radius/axis

sources.title: This robotic tentacle can easily grasp smooth objects (MIT Technology Review, 2017)
sources.what_it_supports: Festo OctopusGripper: pneumatic silicone tentacle curls inward, two rows of vacuum suction cups

source_note: Bending-angle range is general PneuNet knowledge; sources opened did not give numbers.

name: Variable-stiffness jamming segments (add-on)
mechanism: A membrane filled with granules (e.g. ground coffee) or layers stiffens when vacuum compacts it, locking the segment shape.
print_notes: End caps/fittings printable; membrane must be bought or cast; TPU membranes leak.
known_issues: bulky and heavy (pump) for a drone

sources.title: How we made an octopus-inspired surgical robot using coffee (Scientific American)
sources.what_it_supports: STIFF-FLOP: ground-coffee granular jamming chamber in silicone pneumatic arm, vacuum switches soft->stiff

sources.title: Variable-stiffness continuum robot review/prototype (Machines 10(7):581)
sources.what_it_supports: Granular jamming background: weak in tension, bulky, buckling during jamming transition; layer-jamming prototype to 60x stiffness at -60 kPa

sources.title: Robotic modules for a continuum manipulator with variable stiffness joints (Sant'Anna)
sources.what_it_supports: Friction-locking alternative to jamming: pressurised pads on ball joint, +95% stiffness at 500 kPa; 0-30 deg/module, 35 mm, 7 g; valves bulky

name: Scissor / Sarrus linkages for extension
mechanism: Stacked Sarrus (or scissor) linkages provide a 1-DOF telescoping stroke with high axial stiffness; usually combined with a bending section.
print_notes: Plates print flat; hinge pins should be steel (printed pins bent and failed); limit hinge to just below full extension to avoid singularity.
known_issues: pin bending/failure after dozens of cycles
spring torque vs actuator torque mismatch

sources.title: Sarrus linkage aerial drone arm (Idaho State Univ. robotics lab)
sources.what_it_supports: Stacked Sarrus links, ABS, 10.2 -> 33 cm (~3.2:1), ~450 g; torsion springs + single cable; pins bent/failed after dozens of cycles; singularity at full extension

sources.title: An extensible continuum robot with integrated origami parallel modules (academia.edu)
sources.what_it_supports: Waterbomb-base origami parallel modules on steel spring backbone; up to 45 deg/module, >180 deg over 6 modules; crease fatigue

name: Parallel continuum / Stewart-like mini segments
mechanism: Several flexible rods or tendon-driven continuum legs join a base to a moving platform, giving multi-DOF motion with higher stiffness than a single serial backbone.
print_notes: Platforms and base print easily; flexible legs should be NiTi, spring steel or carbon rod; printed TPU legs too floppy.

sources.title: Singularity analysis of 3-DOF planar parallel continuum robots (Frontiers Robot. AI 2023)
sources.what_it_supports: Parallel continuum robots: continuum legs + passive joints, constant-curvature model; type I/II singularities; loads/instability not modelled

sources.title: Design of the new modular tendon-driven manipulator TENDRIM (TU Braunschweig)
sources.what_it_supports: Bearing-based pitch+roll joints per module (universal-joint equivalent); working range ~120 deg pitch, +/-60 deg roll limited by tendon-link collision; all tendons must stay in tension

source_note: Range taken from TENDRIM pitch/roll working limits (modular tendon-driven parallel-type module).

name: Chain / drag-chain-like interlocking links
mechanism: Links interlock with hard stops (like a cable carrier or keyed vertebrae) so the chain bends freely in one plane to a fixed minimum radius and resists twist and back-bending.
print_notes: Many printable drag-chain designs exist; snap pins must be PETG/nylon; stop-dogs set the bend limit - print with layers perpendicular to stop impact.
known_issues: stops make bending discrete and jerky

sources.title: Cable carriers: review of options to handle cables and hoses (Machine Design)
sources.what_it_supports: Drag-chain link construction, stop-dogs, bend radius set by cable (5-10x OD), polygon crimping when too tight; 3D robot carriers twist/coil 540 deg

sources.title: Multi-material 3D printed tendon-driven continuum segment (Leeds, ICRA preprint)
sources.what_it_supports: Vertebrae on Tango+ backbone; v0.2 soft hinges alternated 90 deg (~15 deg/vertebra, 135 deg total); keyed vertebrae cut torsional play 5.6->1.4 deg/vertebra; payload 0.4-1.3 kg; key-base fracture under torsion; nylon then 0.7 mm braided steel tendons

source_note: Per-link angle is typical drag-chain geometry, not from a tentacle paper.

name: Twisted-string actuated joints
mechanism: A motor twists two or more strings so they shorten, giving a high-ratio linear pull that can drive a tendon joint without gearbox.
print_notes: Motor mounts and string terminations print easily; strings must be bought.

sources.title: Twisted string actuators: life cycle, twisting inside Bowden cables, passive return (KAIST)
sources.what_it_supports: No reliable TSA life model; twisting inside Bowden adds friction/hysteresis; one-way pull needs return spring or buckling element; nonlinear contraction

sources.title: Twisted string actuator with load-adaptive transmission (Actuators 13(12), DOAJ record)
sources.what_it_supports: TSA converts motor rotation to pull with high ratio; variable-ratio design applied to robot finger (2.1-6.2x ratio change)

name: Bowden tendon routing friction (actuation side)
mechanism: Tendons run in sheaths from base-mounted servos to the joints; friction follows the capstan law T_out = T_in * exp(-mu * total wrap angle), so cumulative sheath bending sets force loss.
print_notes: Printed guides should be PTFE-lined or use steel guide pins/pulleys; avoid routing tendons through raw printed holes (layer ridges abrade lines).
known_issues: exponential tension loss with total bend angle (mu 0.2-0.3 typical examples)
distal segment tendons pass through proximal ones (coupling)

sources.title: Cable mechanism maths: designing against the capstan equation (Hackaday 2021)
sources.what_it_supports: T_load/T_hold = exp(mu*theta), cumulative bend angle counts; mu 0.2-0.3 examples; minimise bends, use pulleys, nylon-coated cable

sources.title: Tendon-driven continuum robots 101 (Open Continuum Robotics, U Toronto)
sources.what_it_supports: Spacer-disk vs lumen designs; >=3 tendons for spatial bending; disk-tendon friction, tendon slack/backlash, one motor set per segment

sources.title: A servo powered robotic arm, but like you've never seen before (Hackaday 2018)
sources.what_it_supports: 8 printed ball-joint segments, 16 remote RC servos, fishing line routed in tubing (Bowden) to decouple joints

name: Octopus-inspired arm references (summary)
mechanism: Tapered, soft or wedge-segmented arms that curl from tip to base to wrap objects; actuation by cables, SMA or pneumatics.
print_notes: SpiRobs is the only octopus-like design here printed on a consumer FDM printer (Bambu, TPU 95A).
known_issues: silicone/SMA arms are slow and heavy for a drone
tendon arms need careful taper vs force trade-off

summary.bend: curls into full log spiral, curvature radius decreases linearly to tip; grasps 5.6-115 mm objects

summary.bend: ~85 deg simple bending; one cable for retroflexion/grasp
